resolution: With no allowlisted schemas, show the named configuration-empty guidance and no action targeting an implicit schema.
While queue/backend observation runs, retain the last complete observed values with their snapshot and expose a named busy refresh control.
A failed queue/backend observation names its unavailable source and reason, retains known evidence, and offers refresh without claiming a remote operation failed.
For a selected schema, show queue and backend observations under separate labels with full schema and index identity; do not roll them into contract or document success.
When only one observation source is available, keep that known result and identify the other source as unavailable instead of substituting zero or healthy.
Schema modules and index names wrap or reflow within the existing selector/result layout; essential identity is not clipped and the page does not gain horizontal overflow.
No configured schema uses the empty guidance; one or many configured schemas keep an explicit selected target and never silently switch actions to a different schema.
Long schema modules, index names, and observation reasons remain readable at narrow widths and are not available only through a tooltip.
Before contract or document checks run, identify each result as not checked; no empty result is presented as a matching contract or present document.
During either check, name the in-flight observation and leave the independent contract/document result visible without changing it to success.
A contract-check or document-observation failure identifies which check could not be checked, retains its reason, and remains unknown rather than a remote task failure.
Show declared-versus-live contract findings and expected-document presence as independent results with their applicable index/document evidence.
If contract evidence is complete but document evidence is unavailable (or vice versa), retain the known result and explicitly label the other one incomplete; one cannot stand in for the other.
Long field names, index names, document identifiers, and mismatch reasons wrap within the named evidence region without hiding row labels or causing page-level horizontal scroll.
Zero mismatches and multiple mismatch rows use explicit counts and the same result structure; zero contract drift never implies that expected documents are present.
Full field/document/index identifiers and mismatch reasons remain selectable and readable without truncating the only evidence.
An accepted recovery check displays progress while preserving its exact queue job/attempt and backend task UID; refreshing checks the same operation and never resubmits it.
Timeout, transport failure, missing task, or malformed evidence says the outcome could not be checked and remains unknown; only authoritative evidence may show remote failure or success.
Long recovery status and reason text wraps beside the complete task/job identity without forcing page-level horizontal scrolling.
Full schema, index, queue job, attempt, and task identifiers remain readable at narrow widths and stay beside their own outcome.
While promotion is accepted or running, retain its exact task UID and live/target index identities, prevent a duplicate submission, and do not call it complete.
Eligibility blocks retain a concrete reason; terminal failed/canceled tasks remain distinct from unknown observation and keep the task UID visible.
The confirmation and promotion result reflow or scroll within their existing named container so full identity and alias-effect text remain visible without page overflow.
The confirmation and result keep full schema, live index, target index, alias effect, and task UID readable without clipping or tooltip-only access.
A non-focus-moving operation status announces the changed progress once, preserves focus, and does not repeat unrelated evidence.
Visible feedback names whether the remote task failed or the observation failed; unknown observation never uses copy or color that asserts remote failure.
Long asynchronous status and error messages wrap within the feedback region and cannot create page-level horizontal overflow or cover their related controls.
Full operation references and their state labels remain visible and readable; no tooltip or color-only cue is required to understand the outcome.
